conventions: `לְדֹר וָדֹר` → *unto all generations* (v10) is read as rule 22's distributive repetition and not as a rule 30 fusion of the three morphemes: the single written `לְ` opens the phrase and takes *unto*, the first `דּוֹר` takes *all generations* together with the supplied determiner standing before it under rule 15, and the waw and the repeated `דּוֹר` are each `unrepresented`. A universal *all* before a plural noun is read as the distributive determiner rule 22 names alongside *every* and *each*, because the English noun is still a word the ASV spends on this noun in particular while the repetition and the coordination are left saying nothing either way. The corpus contains both treatments — the split at EXO.3.15 and PRO.27.24 among others, the fusion at PSA.106.31 and ISA.58.12 — so the choice is recorded here rather than promoted.

Rule 43's count of the morphemes that could carry a supplied *have* was run twice in this chapter with opposite outcomes, and both stand. At v5 *hath* is `added`: the clause writes no `הָיָה` and no existential particle, and the `בְ` and the suffix have each already been spent on *for* and *his*, so nothing is left for the word to complete. At v2 no part of *have any being* is `added`: it is the whole of `עוֹד`'s own rendering, headed on *being* under rule 31, and dropping it leaves that morpheme with no English at all. A later verse should run the subtraction rather than reading either verse as the chapter's policy on a supplied *have*.
report: Cross-verse: no construction is analysed two ways without something in the source licensing the difference. The candidate lemmas all resolve to ASV wording choices over different source contexts — `לְ` *for*/*unto*/*to*, `בְ` *in* (object of trust, v3) vs *for* (beth essentiae, v5) vs *while* (temporal clause, v2), `הַ` written *The* (v6) vs unrepresented beside a single written determiner (v4), `שֶׁ` *whom* with a written antecedent (v3) vs *he that* headless (v5, rule 46's first rider), `שָׁמַר` *keepeth*/*preserveth*, `עָשָׂה` *made*/*executeth*.

Participle policy is uniform across the three-colon runs: an anarthrous participle carries its supplied *Who*, *the* or *them that* into its own unit (v6 s001, v7 s001/s006/s013, v8 s003/s006/s009, v9 s011, rule 46); the one articular participle gives the relative to the article and keeps its own verb (v6 s014/s015, rule 41); a participle standing with an explicit written subject takes no relative at all (v7 s012, v8 s002/s008, v9 s002).

I read the dump for the split the lemma table cannot show — a supplied word marked `added` in one verse and folded in elsewhere. The four `added` units each survive the check: v3 *your* is a supplied possessive on the light verb's complement, which rule 44 sends to rule 18's closing sentence (`הָלַךְ` → *go* ***your way***); v4 *very* is an intensifier no morpheme says, the demonstrative already holding the one written determiner; v5 *hath* fails rule 43's count because `בְ` holds *for* and the suffix *his*, exactly as rule 43's own `אוֹ תְבַלֻל בְעֵינוֹ` example; v8 *the eyes of* is a supplied object noun that does not write `פָּקַח`'s lexeme, kept as one run under rule 2.

The apparent counter-case is v2's *have any being*, folded into `עוֹד` rather than marked `added` beside v5's *hath*. That is rule 43's own subtraction and not an inconsistency: in v5 every morpheme of the clause already holds an English word, while dropping *have any being* leaves `עוֹד` with nothing at all. Recorded as a convention so a later verse runs the test rather than copying either outcome.

BSB: 4 disagreements out of 114 comparable occurrences, all documented convention differences and none an error. PSA.146.3 `וֹ` is the resumptive suffix left unwritten because the ASV wrote *in whom* as two words (rule 22); PSA.146.4 `הַ֙` is the agreement article beside a single written determiner (rules 41, 47); PSA.146.10 `וָ` and `דֹר` are the waw and repeated noun of the distributive repetition (rule 22). BSB attaches each to its own phrase, which is the difference rule 22 already records.

No promotion. The one construction that might have taught a rule — `לְדֹר וָדֹר` → *unto all generations*, where the distributive determiner is a universal *all* with a plural noun rather than rule 22's *every* or *each* — is treated both ways in the finished corpus: 5 units align a single `דּוֹר` to *all generations* with 9 `unrepresented` seconds, against 2 `noncompositional` three-morpheme fusions at PSA.106.31 and ISA.58.12. A corpus that contradicts itself here is a reason not to promote, so the chapter's reading is recorded as a convention instead.
Ledger checks clean in the report: 128 units, all 124 source and 168 target IDs partitioned once, every recorded head a member of its unit.
